# Storefront Platform Design Spec — Sub-project #6

**Date:** 2026-05-17
**Author:** Generated by Claude Opus 4.7 in dialogue with operator
**Status:** Locked-in scope, ready for implementation
**Implements:** [Sub-project #6 plan](../plans/2026-05-17-storefront.md)

## 1. Goal

Turn the existing 4-protocol landing-page deployment (`v0.5`) into a **complete clinical-skincare DTC storefront**:

- A real homepage at `/` instead of a redirect
- An AI triage funnel that recommends a protocol based on a selfie
- A brand-story page that establishes the brand's clinical authority (GMC registration, ISO 22716 manufacturing, etc.)
- An individual-product catalog (currently only bundles are sold)
- A persistent unified cart that carries bundles + individual products together
- A universal checkout page used by all flows
- Order tracking for customers
- Contact, legal pages, and SEO foundations

After this sub-project, a visitor can: discover Clarté MD without knowing the URL → pick or be guided to a protocol → optionally add à la carte products → check out in one place → track their order. None of these flows exist today.

## 2. Non-goals (explicitly out of scope)

The following are intentionally deferred to future sub-projects:

- **Customer accounts** (signup/login, order history, saved addresses) — sub-project #8
- **Newsletter subscriber UI + double-opt-in flows** — sub-project #7 (the `subscribers` DB table lands here but the UI is minimal)
- **Reviews aggregation page** — sub-project #7
- **Blog / journal / ingredient deep-dive content** — sub-project #9
- **Loyalty / referral / discount codes** — sub-project #10
- **Urdu language toggle + WCAG accessibility audit** — sub-project #11
- **Customer support inbox** — out of scope; ops handles WhatsApp directly
- **Subscriptions / replenishment reminders** — sub-project #10
- **Multi-currency display (USD for diaspora)** — sub-project #11
- **A/B testing infrastructure** — operator can wire GTM-side for now

## 3. Tech stack

No new core dependencies. Adds two minor libraries:

| Library | Purpose | Status |
|---|---|---|
| `next-mdx-remote` | Render the 4 legal pages from MDX with versioning | NEW dependency |
| `react-hook-form` | Optional — for the unified `<CheckoutForm />` if state-management gets gnarly | NEW optional dependency |

Otherwise: Next.js 15 App Router, Supabase, Drizzle ORM, Zod, Vercel — exactly as today.

## 5. Data model changes

### New table: `subscribers`

```sql
CREATE TABLE subscribers (
  id          uuid PRIMARY KEY DEFAULT gen_random_uuid(),
  email       text NOT NULL UNIQUE,
  source_page text,                         -- 'homepage', 'footer', 'quiz-exit', etc.
  ip_hash     text NOT NULL,                -- anti-spam, same hash pattern as ai_sessions
  created_at  timestamp WITH TIME ZONE DEFAULT now()
);
CREATE INDEX subscribers_created_at_idx ON subscribers (created_at);
```

For now the only place this gets written from is the contact form (optional newsletter checkbox) and a footer newsletter stub. Full subscriber UX is sub-project #7.

### Existing schema unchanged

`orders`, `order_items`, `products`, `bundles`, `bundle_items`, `ai_sessions` all stay as-is. No migrations needed beyond `subscribers`.

## 6. Cart model

### State shape

```ts
// lib/cart/types.ts
export type CartItem =
  | { type: 'bundle'; slug: string; qty: 1 }   // bundle qty is always 1 (mental model: one regimen)
  | { type: 'product'; sku: string; qty: number };

export interface Cart {
  items: CartItem[];
  createdAt: number; // ms epoch — for clearing stale carts after N days
}
```

### Persistence

- localStorage key: `clarte_cart_v1`
- On load, parse + validate via Zod. Drop unknown shape → empty cart.
- On any mutation, write back.
- 14-day TTL — carts older than that get cleared on load.

### Why localStorage (vs cookie / Supabase)

| Option | Pros | Cons | Decision |
|---|---|---|---|
| localStorage | Simple, no server roundtrip, works offline | Per-device, lost when storage cleared | ✅ v1 |
| Cookie | Survives across tabs, server-readable | 4KB limit, GDPR consent banner needed | ❌ |
| Supabase row | Cross-device persistence | Requires anonymous session or signup | ❌ defer to sub-project #8 |

### Cart operations

```ts
// lib/cart/operations.ts
export function addBundle(cart: Cart, slug: string): Cart;     // replaces existing bundle with same slug
export function addProduct(cart: Cart, sku: string, qty?: number): Cart;
export function removeItem(cart: Cart, idx: number): Cart;
export function updateQty(cart: Cart, idx: number, qty: number): Cart;
export function clearCart(cart: Cart): Cart;
```

### Cart provider

```ts
// lib/cart/provider.tsx — React Context wrapping the above
export function useCart(): { cart: Cart; add: ..., remove: ..., update: ..., clear: ... };
```

Mounted in `app/layout.tsx` so every page can read/write.

## 7. Checkout model

### One source of truth: `<CheckoutForm />`

Extracted from the current `/acne` inline intake form. Becomes a reusable React component that:

- Renders the same fields (name, phone, email, address, city, postal, notes, payment radio)
- Validates via Zod (`CreateOrderSchema`)
- Submits to `POST /api/create-order` with the current cart contents
- On success, navigates to a thank-you page (`/order/[number]?phone=XXXX`)
- On failure, shows the same inline error UX as today

Used in:
- `/checkout` (driven by cart contents) — PRIMARY
- All 4 protocol pages? **No.** The protocol pages drop their inline forms and become CTA-driven (Add bundle → /checkout).

### Why no inline form on protocol pages

The user chose "Universal /checkout for everything". The trade-off was: inline forms convert better for one-shot funnels (paid traffic), but maintaining two checkout flows doubles code + risk. Decision: trust that cart → /checkout is a small enough step that conversion stays acceptable. Re-evaluate after 4 weeks of data.

### `POST /api/create-order` payload extension

Current payload:

```json
{
  "items": [{ "sku": "clear-skin-protocol", "name": "...", "qty": 1, "price": 6499 }],
  ...
}
```

Items array is already generic. The extension is: support items where `sku` is an individual product (e.g. `vitc`, not `*-protocol`). The route already handles this via `isBundle: i.sku.endsWith('-protocol')`. No backend change needed beyond validating individual SKUs exist in the products table.

## 9. Component contracts

### `<SiteHeader />`

```tsx
interface SiteHeaderProps {
  // No props; reads cart count from context
}
```

Renders:
- Logo (left)
- Desktop nav: Protocols ▾ (dropdown listing 4) · Products · Quiz · About (center)
- Mobile: hamburger menu (right)
- Cart icon with badge (right)

Sticky at top, ~64px tall, white background w/ subtle bottom border.

### `<SiteFooter />`

```tsx
interface SiteFooterProps {
  // No props
}
```

Renders 4 columns + bottom strip:
- Protocols — links to 4 protocol pages
- Help — Contact, Order tracking, Returns, Shipping
- Legal — Privacy, Terms
- Newsletter — email input + "Subscribe" button (stub for v1; future-wired to subscribers table)
- Bottom strip: copyright + "Made in Lahore" + ISO/GMP badges

### `<CartProvider />`

```tsx
interface CartProviderProps {
  children: React.ReactNode;
}
```

Manages cart state, hydrates from localStorage on mount, persists on every change. Children access via `useCart()`.

### `<QuizFlow />`

```tsx
interface QuizFlowProps {
  // No props
}
```

State machine:
- `idle` → user sees upload UI
- `consent` → consent checkbox + "Analyze" CTA
- `loading` → progress UI (~15-30s)
- `result` → shows analysis + "Start the X Protocol" CTA + "These also help" secondary
- `error` → upload-retry + WhatsApp consult fallback

Calls `POST /api/ai/analyze-skin` (existing endpoint). No new backend.

### `<CheckoutForm />`

Receives cart contents from `useCart()`. Submits to `POST /api/create-order`. Reuses validation patterns from current acne intake.

### `<OrderSummary />`

```tsx
interface OrderSummaryProps {
  cart: Cart;
  showPlaceOrderButton: boolean;
}
```

Renders the current acne sidebar — line items + discount + shipping + total. Used in `/cart` (without button) and `/checkout` (with button).

### `<ProductCard />` + `<BundleCard />`

```tsx
interface ProductCardProps {
  product: Product; // from Drizzle Product type
}
interface BundleCardProps {
  bundle: Bundle;
  items: Product[]; // resolved bundle members
}
```

Image, name, actives, price, list price (with strikethrough if discounted), "Add to cart" button.

## 10. API endpoint specs

### `GET /api/products/[sku]`

```ts
// Response:
{
  ok: true,
  product: {
    sku, name, pricePkr, listPricePkr, actives, imageUrl, active, createdAt
  }
}
// or 404 with { ok: false, error: "Not found" }
```

Public, cached at the edge. No rate limit needed.

### `POST /api/cart/preview`

```ts
// Body:
{
  items: CartItem[]
}
// Response:
{
  ok: true,
  items: Array<{ sku, name, qty, unit_price_pkr, line_total_pkr, is_bundle }>,
  totals: { subtotal_pkr, shipping_pkr, total_pkr },
  free_shipping_threshold_pkr: 4000,
  free_shipping_remaining_pkr: 1500  // or 0 if already over
}
```

Server-side authoritative — resolves bundles to their member products, validates SKUs exist, applies free-shipping rule. Same defense as `/api/create-order`'s total recomputation.

### `GET /api/order/[number]?phone=XXXX`

```ts
// Verifies last 4 digits of phone match the stored phone for that order_number.
// Response on match:
{
  ok: true,
  order: {
    order_number, status, created_at, items, totals, customer_name_first_only,
    shipping_city, payment_status
  }
}
// Response on mismatch or not found:
{ ok: false, error: "Order not found or phone doesn't match" }
// (Don't leak whether the order exists.)
```

Rate-limited via existing IP-hash mechanism (10/hr per IP).

### `POST /api/contact`

```ts
// Body:
{
  name: string,
  email: string,
  phone: string,
  message: string,
  subscribe?: boolean  // newsletter opt-in
}
// Response:
{ ok: true }
```

- Validates via Zod
- Rate-limits via IP (5/hr — same as AI rate limit)
- Fires `WEBHOOK_CONTACT_SUBMITTED` (operator wires to email + ops Slack)
- If `subscribe` is true, inserts into `subscribers` table
- Doesn't persist contact submissions to DB by default (webhook is the source of truth)

## 11. Migration strategy

### Existing protocol pages

Each of `/acne`, `/even-tone`, `/renewal`, `/barrier` undergoes the same transformation:

1. Wrap with `<SiteHeader />` + `<SiteFooter />`
2. Replace inline `<form id="orderForm">` with a button that calls `useCart().add({ type: 'bundle', slug })` then routes to `/checkout`
3. Remove the bundled order-summary `<aside>` (now lives in `/cart` and `/checkout`)
4. Keep all other content (hero, rx-strip, reviews, FAQ, sticky-CTA, etc.) intact — these are the conversion patterns from sub-project #5 phase 2 and they stay

### Backward compatibility

- `POST /api/create-order` already handles cart payloads (just with bundle-only items currently). Mixed-cart payloads work without backend changes beyond SKU validation extending to individual products.
- Webhooks (`WEBHOOK_ORDER_*`) fire identically whether order came from a protocol page or `/checkout`. The `order.source_page` field captures origin.
- Admin panel (`/admin/orders`) is unchanged — it already reads any order regardless of source.

### Cart-state migration

If a returning visitor has a `clarte_cart_v1` from this version and we change the shape later, the CartProvider's load function rejects unknown shapes and starts fresh. Acceptable v1 trade-off.

## 12. Decisions made

| Question | Choice | Rationale |
|---|---|---|
| Universal `/checkout` vs hybrid? | Universal | Operator chose this — less code, single source of truth. Risk noted in §7. |
| Quiz scope | Single-screen | Operator chose simplest path; iterate if conversion data warrants. |
| SEO scope | Foundation only | Operator chose; blog deferred to sub-project #9. |
| Cart persistence | localStorage | Simpler than cookie or Supabase row; acceptable per-device limitation. |
| Cart line model | Bundle as single line | "One regimen" mental model matches how the brand sells. |
| Order tracking auth | Phone last-4 | No real auth needed for v1; deters basic brute force. Full auth is sub-project #8. |
| Contact form storage | Webhook only, not DB | Operator's CRM is the source of truth. Don't duplicate. |
| Newsletter signup | DB row + optional webhook | Subscribers list is operator's asset; persist locally. |

## 13. Success criteria

For the operator to call sub-project #6 done, the following must all be true:

1. `https://lp.clartemd.com.pk/` renders a homepage (not a redirect)
2. The 4 protocol pages still convert end-to-end (now cart-driven)
3. A visitor can take the AI quiz from `/`, get a recommended protocol, click through, and complete an order
4. A visitor can browse `/products`, view a product detail page, add to cart, check out
5. A visitor can mix-add (e.g. acne bundle + retinol serum à la carte) and check out in one flow
6. `/order/CLM-2026-XXXX?phone=XXXX` shows the order to the right person and refuses wrong phones
7. `/contact` form submits and triggers `WEBHOOK_CONTACT_SUBMITTED`
8. All 4 legal pages render with reviewable content
9. `sitemap.xml`, `robots.txt`, OG meta, Schema.org markup all present and valid (Lighthouse SEO score 95+)
10. All current `lp.clartemd.com.pk/admin/orders` operations still work
11. Full test suite (lint + unit + integration + E2E) green
12. `npm run build` succeeds; deploy to prod via Vercel; `v0.6` tagged

## 16. Risks + mitigations

| Risk | Mitigation |
|---|---|
| Universal checkout reduces protocol-page conversion | Track conversion before/after via GTM; if drop >15%, revert protocol pages to inline forms (~4h rollback) |
| Cart state corrupts mid-flow | Strict Zod validation on load; clear on parse failure |
| Mixed-cart total computation diverges between client and server | Single source of truth is server (`/api/cart/preview` + `/api/create-order` re-computes); UI only displays |
| New homepage doesn't rank for "Clarté MD" branded search | Ship with explicit `<title>Clarté MD — Dermatologist-led skincare</title>` and Organization schema |
| Quiz fails on slow PK mobile networks | Show progressive loading states; fail gracefully with WhatsApp consult fallback |
| Operator can't supply doctor portrait in time | Phase B includes a placeholder hero variant; brand-anonymous "Our GMC-registered doctor" works without a photo |
| Legal pages have legally-binding errors | Operator-blocked: must have lawyer review before public launch; placeholder text is clearly marked |
